- **Agent:** queue worker (repo-worker-code), Lane D shift

- **Item (2) status:** PR #3018 (head 1108a7509) — Codex re-review clean on current head (2026-10-31T11:31Z, no findings); CI still pending (mcpx run 41197053379 pending, mcpx-docs build queued) under the current fleet CI congestion. Merge as soon as those go green.
- **Item (1) design finding (verified against the pinned v2 source this shift):** `mcp.transform` is NOT a per-session surface. In the pinned plugin API (`packages/plugin/src/promise/mcp.ts`) it is `Transform<MCPEditor>` over the location-wide server registry (list/get/set/update/remove over `Mcp.ServerConfig`), and in core (`packages/core/src/mcp/index.ts`, `plugin/host.ts`) the callbacks re-run on registry reconcile/reload. The callback is synchronous, so it cannot query the daemon; the established pattern (core `config/plugin/policy.ts`, `config/plugin/mcp.ts`) is a callback closing over asynchronously-refreshed state. So item (1) as worded ("filtered server set per session") needs one semantics decision before implementation: e.g. (a) the transform removes registry servers the mcpx daemon catalog marks unmanaged/disabled, closing over daemon status refreshed by the plugin; or (b) it registers the daemon's live servers into the registry (needs the config shape mcpx-as-MCP-server takes in opencode config, which the v2 docs do not yet specify). Implementing either blind would risk the plugin deleting or duplicating a user's hand-configured servers — the declared-but-broken failure mode this repo guards against. Next implementer: pick (a)/(b) on this issue first, then implement in the permission.ts pattern (pure filter function over the editor + wiring that hands out the filter only after registration succeeds).
- **Expectation:** task parked on PR #3018 CI; on resume, merge #3018 when green, then take the item (1) semantics decision above.

- **Agent:** repo queue worker, lane code-h (repo-worker-code)
- **Session / ID:** cron repo-queue-worker-shift-h run 2026-11-08; task 13615
- **Task:** task 13615 for issue #2841 — SET-REMAINDER item (3), the TUI `select()` daemon picker.
- **Outcome:** PR #7847 opened: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7847 (branch `queue/13615-2841-daemon-picker`, commit 884ad6fbf5).

**Deviation — the pinned v2 surface cannot support a true TUI select.** Verified 2026-11-08 against the pinned opencode fork (`~/git/opencode` at `ededbacbfd`, `@opencode/plugin` version 2.0.30):

- `packages/plugin/src/promise/plugin.ts`: the setup `Context` has a fixed domain list (agent, aisdk, command, credential, event, integration, mcp, messaging, model, generate, permission, plugin, provider, reference, rpc, session, shell, skill, storage, tool, vcs, websearch, worktree) — no ui/tui/question domain, and no select/dialog/prompt method on any domain a server plugin receives. The `question` tool is a built-in model tool (`codemode: false`), not a plugin surface.
- The v1 picker (`mcpx-tui.tsx`) exists only because v1 has a separate TUI plugin realm (`@opencode-ai/plugin/tui`, `DialogSelect`); the v2 module contract (`{ id, setup }` / `{ id, effect }`) has no TUI counterpart in the pin.

**Closest supported equivalent landed in PR #7847:** the `mcpx_daemon_pick` tool. With no index it renders the picker menu (ranked candidates, in-use daemon marked, config path + detail per option — the v1 DialogSelect options as data). With an index it asserts `mcpx_daemon_select` through the permission domain with daemon_select's payload, and only a confirmed selection reaches the ctx.storage-backed apply (remember.ts). Cancellation, invalid indexes, picker errors, and a missing permission domain apply nothing. Targeted tests: `bun test plugin/opencode/v2/` — 73 pass, 0 fail (baseline 61), including a stub-storage oracle proving a confirmed pick persists and a cancelled pick mutates nothing.

Item (5) v1 retirement is not in PR #7847; it stays sequenced after item (3) lands or is waived. The same deviation is recorded on #1858.
- **Links:** task 13615 · issue #2841 · issue #1858 · PR #7847
